APPLICATION OF Ellen Vison FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Leo Paul Hamner IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT CUSHMAN AGENCY TACOMA, WASHINGTON NAME OF AGENCY FROM WHICH PUPIL CAME: Flathead Date of enrollment, Sept. 5, 1918 Term of enrollment, three (3) years. NAME OF PERSON ARRANGING FOR THE TRANSFER: Theo. Sharp Position, Sup't APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the Government of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Tacoma, Washington, I hereby certify that I have this day carefully examined the above-named child herein proposed for transfer and find him to be in proper physical condition to attend school, and not afflicted with tuberculosis or any disease which would be a menace to the health of other pupils. This ____________ day of ____________, 191 Physician at ___________________________ Agency. CERTIFICATE OF AGENT OR BONDED SUPERINTENDENT. I hereby certify that the statements made in the foregoing application and certificate, to the best of my knowledge and belief, are true; that the consent of ___________________________ (Parent, guardian, or next of kin) was voluntary. (Here state whether the child lives within reach of a public school, whether the State laws permit it to enroll therein, and if it lives near the public school why it can not attend such school.) I recommend the transfer of the said child. This ____________ day of ____________, 191 Agent or Superintendent. CERTIFICATE OF SCHOOL PHYSICIAN. I hereby certify that on Oct. 10 - 1919, I made a careful examination of the physical condition of Leo Paul Harmer, the child named in the foregoing application, and found him to be in proper physical condition to attend school. I therefore recommend that the said child be enrolled in this school. This 10th day of Oct., 1919 School Physician. SPECIAL NOTE. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parent is living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. Applicable laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 731.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. Compliance must be given to all orders and instructions promulgated in connection with the new course of study issued December 1, 1915. The information as to public school facilities called for in the certificate of the Superintendent (third page hereof) must be given, and all superintendents are especially directed to exhaust every means to secure enrollment of Indian children in the State public schools, pursuant to instructions heretofore issued in this regard. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Jan. 7, 1920 Mr. Theodore Sharp, Supt. Flathead Indian Agency Dixon, Montana Sir: There is enclosed herewith Official Receipt No. 176146 covering deposit of $20.00 for Leo Paul Hummer by his mother Helen Vincent. Mrs. Vincent sent this money for Leo's fare home. Kindly forward this receipt to Mrs. Vincent. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. :MG Enc. Menager's Cash Store Ronan, Montana 1/15 1920 Mr. E.H. Hammond Superintendent Dear Sir, On Dec 5th I sent you cheque for 20.00 to send my boy Leo Paul Hammer home as yet you have not replied to my letter or acknowledge receipt of cheque. I'd like to hear from you. If you do not feel inclined to let him come home kindly give him the money for spending money. Yours Truly, Helen Vincent Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Jan. 19, 1920 Mrs. Helen Vincent Ronan, Montana Dear Madam: In answer to your letter of December 5th, it is to the best interests of your son, Leo Paul Hamner, that he remains at Cushman School to the end of the school year to get the full benefit of this year's instruction. For this reason, the money you sent for his return was not given to him. On January 6, I issued a receipt in your name placing $20.00 to the credit of your son on my books. This receipt was mailed to Superintendent Sharp on January 7th for delivery to you. The money will be given to Leo in small sums from time to time for his spending money. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. CHK:MG Cushman Indian School Mr. E.H. Hammond I enclose you 20¢ that you may if you will buy a F.R.R. ticket for my boy Leo Paul Hamme. I have made arrangements with Mr. Sharp (Ind. Sup't) that he might attend school here. I'm not well and want my boy when I can see him. Yours Respectfully Helen Vincent Mrs. E.H. Hammond Dear sir, I am writing after lines to ask you for my boy Leo. What don't you let him out from Cushman let him come will I don't want to pay $200 per annum or $20 a month at sir give him the money and let him go. That is all for this time next time I'll be there so good by and good luck sir. I am yours, from Helen Vincent Ronan Montana Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Oct. 15, 1919 Mrs. Helen Vincent Ronan, Montana Dear Madam: Replying to your letter of October 11th: As I wrote you, your son is entitled to enter Cushman free of tuition, provided you are not able to pay tuition. Leo was sent to Cushman Indian School for three years and you will be required to keep him here for that length of time at least, unless there are reasons why his enrollment should be cancelled. If you have a good public school in which to enroll him, I will excuse him for that purpose, on the recommendation of your Superintendent. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Flathead Agency, Dixon, Montana. July 21, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt., Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Sir: Ellen Vinson advises me that she has sent money for the return of Peter Pascal Hammer. If it is not your desire to let this boy return home this summer, kindly return the funds which she has advanced. Very respectfully, [signature] Theodore Shap Superintendent. M/P Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., July 28, 1919 Mr. Theodore Sharp, Supt. Flathead Indian Agency Dixon, Montana. Dear Mr. Sharp: I have held Leo Paul Hamner at school as I was under the impression that he was included in the category with the Parisseau boys. Leo is still here and appears to be enjoying himself. I let the boys go out every other day to pick berries or to do other work for wages. They have not complained about hard work or anything else so far as I can learn. Leo and Antoine Parisseau were out last Friday, Saturday and Sunday and have asked permission to go next Saturday and Sunday. I understand that Pat Parisseau has finally reached home. He was granted permission to work in the country on alternating days and broke faith. I am returning herewith the money sent to Leo by Ellen Vinson. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG Enc. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., June 26, 1919 Mrs. Helen Vincent Ronan, Montana Dear Madam: I regret to inform you that there are no funds available for the return of your son, Leo Paul Hammer. Very truly yours, [signature] Superintendent. EHH:MG Dear Sir, if it is all right for him to come back I will send you the money for his RR fare. I need him and would like for him to come home. Ellen Vincent THE MENAGERS CASH RONAN, MONTANA 6/43 1919 Mr. Superintendent Dear Sir, Kindly send my boy back Leo Paul Hammer, and I will refund you the R.R. fare when I get my money in July. The harvest crop is ready and I need his labor as labor is very scarce. Yours Truly, Helen Vincent Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., June 26, 1919 Mrs. Helen Vincent Ronan, Montana Dear Madam: I regret to inform you that there are no funds available for the return of your son, Leo Paul Hammer. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EBH:MG THE MENAGERS CASH RONAN, MONTANA 12/27/1918 Cushman Agency Gentlemen I received by mail an envelope from you empty. You either failed to put letter inside or letter fell out and got lost. Kindly duplicate it. Yours truly, Mrs. Helen Vincent Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Dec. 24, 1918. Mrs. Helen Vincent, Ronan, Montana. Dear Madam: Replying to your letter to your son Leo Paul Hammer relative to returning home for the Christmas holidays, will advise you that owing to the prevalence of influenza and pneumonia this year, it is advisable to keep the children in school to avoid exposure to the disease. There are 325 children at Cushman whose lives should be protected, and it is my duty to use every precaution to keep them from danger. We have gone through one siege of the flu and we will do our utmost to keep from going through another. We have a whole week of games and entertainment planned for the children here and we expect to give them a Turkey dinner, altogether I believe they will have a pleasant holiday. Very sincerely yours, Superintendent Rozan Mont. Oct. 2, 1919 My dear Leo, I sent you this money for to come home. I don't want to pay 200 dollars a year. You come back here and go to school in Rozan. This money for your fare when you come home. I am not feel good today. Well, that is all for this time. Good Bye. I wish you can back soon. Reproduced at the National Archives at Seattle Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Oct. 11, 1919 Mrs. Ellen Vinson Rozan, Montana Dear Mrs. Vinson: I am returning the money order for $25.00 which you sent to Leo, urging him to return home, under the impression that he had to pay a tuition fee of $200.00 a year. Regulations require Indian parents, able to pay tuition, to do it, but Mr. Sharp, your Superintendent, in answer to a letter of inquiry from me wrote that Leo should remain at Cushman. You will therefore not have to pay tuition unless you are able to do so. If you were able to pay tuition, Mr. Sharp would have advised me. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG Enc. Copy to Mr. Sharp. Mr. Leo P. Harmoner 90 Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash. July 20th Rosenmont Dear Brother, I am at home now. I am going with Maggie. Maggie went back to this home and she wants to go with him and I don't like to this place and I want to know if you got that money from your mother. Are you going home sometimes? We are not sure Mr. Harmoner won't let you go and you must tell me what you are doing. July th 120 From you Brother P. M. Kosan Mont Come home will you Leo. Well Leo only he was not good then was bum great like I know please like home of course, and your girl said here your girl honey home well your horse his all right nice and fat. Well now is Bot and anton Valle and antone P. LLC I said hello to everyone. Let me know what pro you never come home it soon. Well I am so so some horny girl right now till a home one girl I said hello honey. Well will be all for the time Leo answer soon SHOE AND HARNESS REPAIRING. RECORD CARD—PREVOCATIONAL DIVISION.
